title: Mutable default argument shares the rejected list between Ingestors
explanation: `rejected: list[Rejection] = []` is evaluated once, so every Ingestor created without an explicit list appends to the same list: rejections of one ingestor show up in all others and the list grows for the life of the process. Use `rejected: list[Rejection] | None = None` and create a new list.

title: Upper limit treated as exclusive although documented inclusive
explanation: LIMITS are documented as both inclusive and the message says `[low, high]`, but the check is `low <= value < high`. A reading with humidity 100 %, temperature 60 C, wind 115 m/s or rain 500 mm is rejected. Saturated air (100 % humidity) is common, so valid readings are dropped. Use `low <= value <= high`.

title: Threshold run is never reset when a reading is back within the limit
explanation: When the value is not past the limit the method returns without clearing `self._runs[station_id]`, contrary to the docstring (a reading within the limit ends the run). Non-consecutive readings are therefore counted as one run (e.g. -1, 5, -1 fires a 2-consecutive frost rule), and because the counter only grows, once it passes `consecutive` the rule can never fire again for that station. Reset the run to 0 on a non-passing reading.

title: Frost counted with <= while frost alert uses <
explanation: frost_readings counts `t <= FROST_LIMIT_C` but frost_rule fires only for `value < limit` ("drops below"). A reading of exactly 0.0 C counts as frost in the daily summary but never raises a frost alert; the two definitions of frost must agree.

title: Circular import between aggregate and alerts
explanation: aggregate imports alerts (only for FROST_LIMIT_C) and alerts imports aggregate (for summarize_all in heavy_rain_days). It works only because both use the other module at call time; any module-level use breaks the import. Shared constants such as FROST_LIMIT_C should live in a lower-level module (models/validation or a constants module) so the dependency goes one way.

title: Quadratic daily aggregation
explanation: summarize_all already groups the readings by station and day, but then calls summarize_day for every station-day, which rescans and re-filters the full readings list each time (readings_for_day). Cost is O(readings x station-days), so a year of data from many stations becomes very slow. Group the readings once (station, day) -> list and summarise each group. The `if summary is not None` branch is also dead because every key has readings.

title: Timezone-aware timestamps crash ingest
explanation: ingest parses taken_at with datetime.fromisoformat, which returns an aware datetime when the payload has an offset (e.g. +02:00). check_timestamp then subtracts a naive `now`, raising TypeError ("can't subtract offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes"). validate is called outside the try block in Ingestor.ingest, so one station payload with an offset raises out of ingest instead of being rejected. Mixed aware/naive readings also crash the sorts in AlertEngine.process and aggregate. Timestamps should be normalised (e.g. to UTC) at ingest.

title: Future-timestamp check is silently skipped by default
explanation: ingest/ingest_batch default `now` to None and validate only runs check_timestamp when now is given, so unless every caller remembers to pass the time, readings stamped arbitrarily far in the future are accepted. The ingestor should default now to the current time (with an injectable clock for tests).

title: Unknown station reported as a malformed payload
explanation: registry.get raises KeyError for an unknown station, which is caught together with real parse errors and recorded as "malformed payload: \"unknown station 's9'\"". The docstring distinguishes unknown stations from malformed payloads; the station lookup should be handled separately so the rejection reason is accurate.

title: No duplicate detection, rain double counted
explanation: A payload re-sent for the same station and taken_at (a common retry after a network failure) is stored again. Since rain_mm is the rain since the previous reading, duplicates are summed into rain_total_mm, inflating daily totals and possibly triggering heavy-rain alerts; temperature mean is skewed too. Reject or replace readings with an already stored (station_id, taken_at).

title: Invalid batches are dropped silently; deeply nested logic
explanation: A batch that is not a dict or has no station_id returns 0 without recording any rejection, so the upload disappears without trace. A `readings` value that is null raises TypeError out of ingest_batch, and a string is iterated character by character. The five levels of nesting make this hard to follow; use early returns/guard clauses and record a Rejection for every refused batch.

title: Path traversal through station_id in export file name
explanation: The output path is built as `folder / f"{station_id}.csv"` without validating station_id. An id such as `../../etc/x` or an absolute path writes outside the export folder, which is synced to a public file share; conversely a crafted path could overwrite arbitrary files. Validate ids against a safe pattern and check that the resolved path stays inside folder. export_daily_csv's `name` parameter has the same problem (line 57).

title: Non-atomic writes into a folder synced to a public share
explanation: Exports are written in place into a folder that the README says is synced to a public file share; the sync can pick up a half-written or truncated CSV. Write to a temporary file in the same folder and os.replace it into place (same for export_daily_csv at lines 58-73).
